headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error: both agents can write files and use network egress, while A’s shared-context skills can be treated as trusted inputs by B.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A exposes shared skill files and a tool-use pattern where skills “reference each other and build on shared context”; Agent B has no documented isolation or provenance checks. That makes instruction smuggling through shared files plausible, though not proven. Because the bridge is indirect and B’s ingestion path is undocumented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF agent_b reads files from the same workspace as agent_a outputs
IF agent_a-generated skill text is parsed as instructions by agent_b
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Add a provenance header to all shared files
Require manual review before B consumes A outputs
Disable automatic skill chaining between agents
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A can read/write files and call APIs; agent B has no documented filesystem access or data classes touched. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class overlap, so leakage is not established. The main concern is limited to accidental exposure if operators manually place files in a common directory.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory
IF sensitive marketing context is stored in files readable by both agents
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Remove sensitive files from any shared path
Check file permissions before running both agents
Keep API credentials out of shared workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; agent B’s write surface is undocumented, but its profile does not rule out overlapping mutable resources. The pair therefore has a plausible conflict path on shared files or state, though not enough evidence for high because B’s write scope is unknown. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF either agent mutates shared git or database state without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Avoid concurrent runs on shared state
Review any git or DB mutations before execution
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A’s shared-context skill design can produce outputs that another agent may treat as authoritative, and agent B has no documented verification or critique step. That creates a plausible cascade where A’s content becomes B’s input and B acts on it without checking. The pathway is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a outputs as source material
IF agent_b forwards or acts on those outputs without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B
Require B to cite source files explicitly
Mark A outputs as untrusted by default
Compare B outputs against original sources
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Agent A touches marketing content and product marketing context; agent B lists no data classes touched. With only docs-only profiles and no compliance-specific fields, a concrete breach is not shown, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into either agent
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter retention policy than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention settings before deployment
Review vendor residency and DPA terms
Log what data classes each agent processes
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
